topic: Kanban in one sentence: the strategy and its three practices

notes.front: What is flow, in The Kanban Guide?
notes.back: The movement of potential value through a system.
notes.explanation: The Guide calls flow central to the definition of Kanban, and its strategy is to optimize value by optimizing flow.
notes.example: A customer request moving from an idea, through building and testing, to something people can use.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Why Use Kanban”, p. 4

notes.front: What are the Kanban practices?
notes.back: Three practices working in tandem: defining and visualizing a workflow; actively managing items in a workflow; improving a workflow.
notes.explanation: They make up the Guide’s definition of Kanban, and the Guide says they work in tandem, meaning together, not as separate options.
notes.example: A team draws its workflow on a wall chart, checks regularly for stuck items, and changes the chart when it finds a better way.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Definition of Kanban”, p. 4

notes.front: What is the Kanban Guide for Scrum Teams?
notes.back: A separate guide, from Scrum.org, Daniel Vacanti and Yuval Yeret (January 2021), for teams using Kanban practices with Scrum.
notes.explanation: It is easy to mistake for The Kanban Guide, but its definition of Kanban and its list of practices differ. Scrum is a lightweight framework in which teams work in fixed-length cycles of one month or less, called Sprints.
notes.example: Like two cookbooks with almost the same title from different publishers: similar ideas, different rules.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide for Scrum Teams (Scrum.org, January 2021), “Definition of Kanban”, p. 3; The Scrum Guide (November 2020), “Scrum Definition” and “The Sprint”

notes.front: What is the Kanban Method?
notes.back: Kanban University’s approach to Kanban: a different body of knowledge from The Kanban Guide.
notes.explanation: It has its own principles and six “general practices”, which are not The Kanban Guide’s three practices.
notes.example: Its practice list includes “Make Policies Explicit” and “Implement Feedback Loops”, which The Kanban Guide does not list.
notes.source: Kanban University, “Kanban Guide” (the Kanban Method), “Kanban General Practices”

notes.front: How does the May 2025 Kanban Guide define Kanban, in one sentence?
notes.back: “Kanban is a strategy for optimizing the flow of value through a process.”
notes.explanation: The exact words matter, because older and rival definitions add phrases such as “pull system”.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Definition of Kanban”, p. 4

notes.front: In its one-line definition, The Kanban Guide describes Kanban as a {{c1::strategy}} for optimizing how value flows through a process.
notes.explanation: The Guide builds on that word: its strategy is to optimize value by optimizing flow.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Definition of Kanban”, p. 4

notes.front: How many practices does The Kanban Guide’s definition of Kanban contain?
notes.back: Three.
notes.explanation: Defining and visualizing a workflow, actively managing items in a workflow, and improving a workflow.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Definition of Kanban”, p. 4

notes.front: The Guide says the three Kanban practices work {{c1::in tandem}}.
notes.explanation: They are meant to operate together, not as separate options to pick from.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Definition of Kanban”, p. 4

notes.front: Two of the Kanban practices are defining and visualizing a workflow, and improving a workflow. What is the third?
notes.back: Actively managing items in a workflow.
notes.explanation: Together the three form the Guide’s definition of Kanban.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Definition of Kanban”, p. 4

notes.front: In their implementation, what are the Kanban practices collectively called?
notes.back: A Kanban system.
notes.explanation: So “Kanban system” means both the Guide’s set of concepts and a team’s working implementation of the three practices.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Definition of Kanban”, p. 4

notes.front: Does the Guide limit Kanban to a particular industry?
notes.back: No. It can work with virtually any workflow, so its application is not limited to any specific industry or context.
notes.explanation: The Guide names knowledge workers in finance, utilities, healthcare and software as examples who have benefited.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Why Use Kanban”, p. 4

notes.front: At what scale does the Guide say Kanban can be used?
notes.back: At any scale, in most contexts where value is delivered.
notes.explanation: The Guide says Kanban can work with virtually any workflow.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Why Use Kanban”, p. 4

notes.front: Three people quote a definition of Kanban. Which one is The Kanban Guide’s current (May 2025) definition?
notes.back: A: a strategy for optimizing the flow of value through a process.
notes.choices:
A) A strategy for optimizing the flow of value through a process
B) A strategy for optimizing the flow of value through a process that uses a visual, work-in-progress limited pull system
C) A strategy for optimizing the flow of value through a process that uses a visual, pull-based system
notes.choicesExplained: B is the Kanban Guide for Scrum Teams (2021). C is the December 2020 Kanban Guide; the 2025 edition simplified it.
notes.explanation: The 2025 edition lists a “simpler definition of Kanban” among its changes.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Definition of Kanban”, p. 4

notes.front: A manager points at a team’s wall chart and says, “That is our Kanban system.” By the Guide, what is the Kanban system?
notes.back: The team’s implementation of all three Kanban practices, not the chart alone.
notes.explanation: A chart supports one practice (defining and visualizing); a Kanban system implements all three together.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Definition of Kanban”, p. 4

notes.front: A team draws its workflow but never manages the items in it or improves it. Is it using Kanban as the Guide defines it?
notes.back: No. Kanban comprises all three practices working in tandem; it has only the first.
notes.explanation: Visualizing without actively managing and improving leaves out two of the three Kanban practices.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Definition of Kanban”, p. 4

notes.front: A team agrees what its units of work are, when each counts as started and finished, and shows this on a wall. Which Kanban practice is that?
notes.back: Defining and visualizing a workflow.
notes.explanation: Deciding what flow means for the team and making it visible is the first practice.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Kanban Practices”, p. 5

notes.front: Every morning a team looks for items that are stuck and works to free them. Which Kanban practice is that?
notes.back: Actively managing items in a workflow.
notes.explanation: The Guide lists unblocking blocked work as one form of active management.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Actively Managing Items in a Workflow”, p. 6

notes.front: After noticing that items wait days for review, a team changes how its workflow is set up. Which Kanban practice is that?
notes.back: Improving a workflow.
notes.explanation: Changing the workflow itself, rather than handling today’s items, is the improvement practice.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Improving the Workflow”, p. 7

notes.front: A water utility’s planning team asks whether Kanban can fit its sector. What does the Guide suggest?
notes.back: It can: the Guide names utilities among the fields whose knowledge workers have benefited from Kanban practices.
notes.explanation: Kanban can work with virtually any workflow and is not limited to any specific industry.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (May 2025), “Why Use Kanban”, p. 4

notes.front: Which document defines Kanban as using “a visual, work-in-progress limited pull system”?
notes.back: The Kanban Guide for Scrum Teams (2021). The May 2025 Kanban Guide’s definition has no such phrase.
notes.explanation: The Kanban Guide stops at “optimizing the flow of value through a process”.
notes.contrast: The Kanban Guide: a strategy for optimizing the flow of value through a process, with three practices.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide for Scrum Teams (Scrum.org, January 2021), “Definition of Kanban”, p. 3

notes.front: How many practices does the Kanban Guide for Scrum Teams list, compared with The Kanban Guide?
notes.back: Four in the Kanban Guide for Scrum Teams; three in The Kanban Guide.
notes.explanation: The Scrum Teams guide lists visualization, limiting work in progress, active management, and inspecting and adapting the Definition of Workflow.
notes.contrast: Don’t carry the Scrum Teams guide’s four practices into answers about The Kanban Guide.
notes.source: The Kanban Guide for Scrum Teams (Scrum.org, January 2021), “Kanban Practices”, p. 4

notes.front: Is “Implement Feedback Loops” one of The Kanban Guide’s practices?
notes.back: No. It is one of the Kanban Method’s six general practices. The Kanban Guide has three practices.
notes.explanation: The Kanban Method is Kanban University’s body of knowledge, separate from The Kanban Guide.
notes.contrast: The Kanban Guide: define and visualize, actively manage, improve.
notes.source: Kanban University, “Kanban Guide” (the Kanban Method), “Kanban General Practices”
notes.sourceLicence: C · all rights reserved (facts only, our wording)

notes.front: The December 2020 Guide defined Kanban as optimizing flow “through a process that uses a visual, pull-based system”. Is that last phrase in the May 2025 definition?
notes.back: No. The 2025 definition ends at “through a process”.
notes.explanation: The 2025 edition lists a “simpler definition of Kanban, specifically as pertains to knowledge work” among its changes.
notes.contrast: 2020: “…through a process that uses a visual, pull-based system”. 2025: “…through a process.”
notes.source: The Kanban Guide (December 2020), “Definition of Kanban”, p. 4
